Tagcast 0.80.0 adds album lyrics import from LRC/TXT files and a choice of fullscreen or in-window Now playing. It also makes the library and metadata editor easier to work with, especially in smaller windows, while keeping the familiar Tagcast layout, controls and review steps.

## Bring your lyrics into an album

Choose **⋯ → Import lyrics…** on an album, then select or drop your LRC/TXT files. Album tracks stay on the left and files on the right. Unique track-number and full-title matches link automatically; uncertain matches stay yours to choose.

Preview the imported text, then review the Before/After values. Existing lyrics are kept unless you explicitly choose to replace them for that track. **Save reviewed lyrics to iBroadcast** requires Premium, checks each track and confirms its save before continuing. Stop, conflicts and uncertain results leave later tracks unsent without automatically retrying.

LRC timestamps are removed: this imports ordinary lyrics text, not synchronised lyrics. Files stay in browser memory until you close the import. Tagcast does not read or modify local music files or contact LRCLIB during this workflow. Supports up to 100 tracks/files, 5 MB in total and 500 KB per file.

## Choose how Now playing opens

**Settings → Interface → Now playing view** offers **Fullscreen** or **In app window**. Fullscreen remains the default; In app window keeps the expanded player inside the current window. Both use the same audio and queue. Escape or Close returns to the library without restarting playback.

The desktop **Help** menu now includes direct links to the Tagcast Reddit community and GitHub home, alongside the Wiki.

## More comfortable browsing and editing

- The compact player keeps Favourite, Dislike, previous/next, Repeat, output and queue controls distinct around narrow-window breakpoints. Longer Repeat labels fit their buttons.
- Tracks remain readable in narrow windows. When the table needs horizontal scrolling, it can be reached and scrolled with the keyboard; wider windows avoid an unnecessary Tab stop.
- Search fields have visible keyboard focus in Light mode. Forest Light has clearer secondary text and focus contrast, with the existing palette retained.
- Selected library overviews use less empty header space. Text categories such as Genres, Tags and Release year show more useful information while artist images and Decades keep their existing presentation.
- The metadata editor has compact tabs, more readable labels and wider online-source queries. Track details stack at narrower widths, and changing tabs preserves your draft and the combined metadata review.
- Artwork comparisons align consistently. Imported lyrics previews follow your selected theme and font.

## Smaller fixes

Imported playlist durations are easier to read and follow the chosen seconds/milliseconds setting. Empty Cleanup previews omit inactive selection and paging controls. Playlist duration columns and singular counts are clearer. Opening Overview directly now refreshes its initial connection message when the library finishes loading.

## Downloads and upgrading

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.80.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.80.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.80.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.80.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Every archive has a SHA-256 companion. **Quit the older Tagcast before upgrading** and keep the complete extracted package together. Settings, sign-in and local account favourites remain in the existing Tagcast folder. Browser-local preferences and Change history remain separate from Electron's profile.

Electron remains the official desktop app; the optional pywebview experiment is not included. On macOS, AirPlay continues to use **System default** with the speaker selected through **Control Centre → Sound**. No native AirPlay playback route or automatic app updater is added.

See the [installation guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/Getting-started) and [full user guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki). Python/browser use remains available. Tagcast never changes local music files.
